metadata.title: Greed is Good: Algorithmic Results for Sparse Approximation
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF→text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.

nodes.name: Dictionary and Atoms
nodes.statement: A dictionary for the signal space $\mathbb{C}^d$ is a finite collection $\{\varphi_\omega\}_{\omega \in \Omega}$ of unit-norm vectors that spans the whole space; its members are called atoms.
nodes.statement_clean: A dictionary is a finite collection of unit-norm spanning vectors called atoms.

nodes.name: Representation and m-term Representation
nodes.statement: A representation of a signal $s$ is a linear combination of atoms equal to $s$ with all coefficients nonzero; an $m$-term representation involves exactly $m$ atoms.
nodes.statement_clean: A representation expresses a signal as a nonzero linear combination of atoms; m-term means m atoms.

nodes.name: $(D,m)$-SPARSE
nodes.statement: Given dictionary $D$ and sparsity $m$, find $\Lambda_m$ and coefficients $\{c_\lambda\}$ minimizing $\|s - \sum_{\lambda \in \Lambda_m} c_\lambda \varphi_\lambda\|_2$ subject to $|\Lambda_m| = m$.
nodes.statement_clean: Find the best m-term linear combination of dictionary atoms approximating a signal in Euclidean norm.

nodes.name: $(D,m)$-EXACT-SPARSE
nodes.statement: Given dictionary $D$ and an input signal $s$ that admits a representation using $m$ atoms or fewer from $D$, recover that sparsest representation.
nodes.statement_clean: Recover the sparsest exact representation of a signal known to be m-sparse over the dictionary.

nodes.name: Matching Pursuit (MP)
nodes.statement: Greedy algorithm that initializes residual $r_0 = s$ and at step $t$ selects the atom most correlated with $r_{t-1}$, updating the approximation and residual.
nodes.origin_citation: Mallat & Zhang 1993; Friedman & Stuetzle 1981 (Projection Pursuit Regression)

nodes.name: Orthogonal Matching Pursuit (OMP)
nodes.statement: Greedy algorithm that selects at each step the atom $\varphi_{\lambda_t}$ best correlated with the residual, then updates the approximant by least-squares projection onto all chosen atoms.
nodes.origin_citation: Chen, Billings, Luo 1989; Pati, Rezaiifar, Krishnaprasad 1993; Davis, Mallat, Zhang 1994

nodes.name: Weak Orthogonal Matching Pursuit (WOMP)
nodes.statement: Variant of OMP that selects at each step an index $\lambda_t$ for which $|\langle r_{t-1}, \varphi_{\lambda_t}\rangle| \geq \alpha \sup_\omega |\langle r_{t-1}, \varphi_\omega\rangle|$ for a fixed weakness parameter $\alpha \in (0,1]$.

nodes.name: Basis Pursuit (BP)
nodes.statement: Convex relaxation that, given an input signal $s$, solves $\min \|b\|_1$ subject to $\sum_\omega b_\omega \varphi_\omega = s$, hoping the nonzero coefficients identify the optimal atoms.
output: Coefficient vector $b$ minimizing $\ell_1$ norm subject to exact reconstruction

nodes.name: Coherence Parameter $\mu$
nodes.statement: The coherence of a dictionary $D$ is $\mu = \max_{\lambda \neq \omega} |\langle \varphi_\lambda, \varphi_\omega\rangle|$, the maximum absolute inner product between two distinct atoms.
nodes.statement_clean: The coherence is the maximum absolute inner product between distinct atoms.

nodes.name: Cumulative Coherence Function $\mu_1(m)$
nodes.statement: For a positive integer $m$, $\mu_1(m) = \max_{|\Lambda| = m} \max_{\psi \notin \Lambda} \sum_{\lambda \in \Lambda} |\langle \psi, \varphi_\lambda\rangle|$, with convention $\mu_1(0)=0$; the dictionary is quasi-incoherent when $\mu_1$ grows slowly.
nodes.statement_clean: Maximum total absolute inner product between an outside atom and any m chosen atoms.

nodes.name: Spark of a Dictionary
nodes.statement: The spark of a dictionary is the least number of atoms that form a linearly dependent set.

nodes.name: Cumulative Coherence Bound by Coherence
nodes.statement: If a dictionary has coherence $\mu$, then $\mu_1(m) \leq m\mu$ for every natural number $m$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.1
nodes.statement: Each absolute inner product is bounded by $\mu$; summing $m$ such terms gives $\mu_1(m) \leq m\mu$.

nodes.name: Dictionary of Decaying Atoms
nodes.statement: For parameter $\alpha \in (0,1)$ and indices $k \in \mathbb{Z}$, define atoms $\varphi_k$ in $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z})$ with geometric decay; the absolute inner product gives coherence $\mu = \alpha$ and explicit closed forms for $\mu_1(m)$ depending on parity of $m$.

nodes.name: Singular Value Lower Bound for Atom Submatrix
nodes.statement: If $\Phi_\Lambda$ is the matrix of $m$ distinct atoms indexed by $\Lambda$, the squared singular values of $\Phi_\Lambda$ exceed $1 - \mu_1(m-1)$.
assumptions: $\Phi_\Lambda$ has columns equal to $m$ distinct unit-norm atoms

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.3 via Gershgorin
nodes.statement: Apply the Gershgorin Disc Theorem to the Gram matrix $\Phi_\Lambda^*\Phi_\Lambda$: each eigenvalue lies in a disc centered at $1$ with radius bounded by $\mu_1(m-1)$, so eigenvalues exceed $1 - \mu_1(m-1)$.

nodes.name: Donoho–Elad/Gribonval–Nielsen Uniqueness via Spark
nodes.statement: A necessary and sufficient condition for every linear combination of $m$ atoms to have a unique $m$-term representation is that $m < \mathrm{spark}(D)/2$.
conclusions: Every linear combination of $m$ atoms has a unique $m$-term representation iff $m < \mathrm{spark}(D)/2$

nodes.name: Donoho–Elad Spark Bounds
nodes.statement: The spark of a dictionary satisfies (1) $\mathrm{spark}(D) > m$ whenever $\mu_1(m-1) < 1$, and (2) $\mathrm{spark}(D) \geq 1 + 1/\mu$.

nodes.name: Gribonval–Nielsen Spark Bound for Multi-ONB
nodes.statement: If $D$ is a $\mu$-coherent dictionary consisting of $L$ orthonormal bases, then a refined lower bound on $\mathrm{spark}(D)$ holds (involving $\mu$ and $L$).

nodes.name: Gilbert–Muthukrishnan–Strauss Approximation for OMP
nodes.statement: Let $D$ have coherence $\mu$ with $8m\mu \leq 1$. For an arbitrary signal $s$, OMP generates an $m$-term approximant $a_m$ satisfying $\|s - a_m\|_2 \leq C\,\|s - a_m^{\mathrm{opt}}\|_2$ where $a_m^{\mathrm{opt}}$ is an optimal $m$-term approximation.
conclusions: OMP gives an $m$-term approximant within a constant factor of optimal

nodes.name: Donoho–Huo Recovery for BP on Two-ONB
nodes.statement: Let $D$ be a union of two orthonormal bases with coherence $\mu$. If $m < (1 + 1/\mu)/2$, then BP recovers every signal that has an $m$-term representation.

nodes.name: Exact Recovery for OMP (Theorem A, part 1)
nodes.statement: A sufficient condition for OMP to recover the sparsest representation of the input signal is $\max_\psi \|\Phi_{\mathrm{opt}}^+ \psi\|_1 < 1$ (ERC), where $\psi$ ranges over the columns of $\Psi_{\mathrm{opt}}$.
assumptions: Signal $s = \Phi_{\mathrm{opt}} c_{\mathrm{opt}}$ uses $m$ linearly independent atoms
conclusions: OMP recovers the optimal atoms and coefficients
OMP is correct for $(D,m)$-EXACT-SPARSE whenever (ERC) holds for every $m$-term signal

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.1 (Exact Recovery for OMP)
nodes.statement: Inductively show that if (ERC) holds, the greedy ratio (largest inner product with optimal atoms vs nonoptimal atoms) exceeds 1 at each step, so OMP recovers an optimal atom each step until all $m$ are found.

nodes.name: Set up greedy ratio
nodes.statement: After $k$ steps, the residual $r_k$ lies in the column span of $\Phi_{\mathrm{opt}}$. The next greedy choice recovers an optimal atom iff the ratio $\|\Psi_{\mathrm{opt}}^* r_k\|_\infty / \|\Phi_{\mathrm{opt}}^* r_k\|_\infty < 1$.

nodes.name: Apply pseudoinverse identity
nodes.statement: Insert $\Phi_{\mathrm{opt}}(\Phi_{\mathrm{opt}}^+)$ into the numerator (a projector onto the column span containing $r_k$) and rewrite the ratio in terms of $\Psi_{\mathrm{opt}}^* (\Phi_{\mathrm{opt}}^+)^* \Phi_{\mathrm{opt}}^* r_k$.

nodes.name: Bound by induced operator norm
nodes.statement: Apply the induced $\ell_\infty \to \ell_\infty$ operator norm bound and switch to $\ell_1 \to \ell_1$ via conjugate transpose, producing $\max_\psi \|\Phi_{\mathrm{opt}}^+ \psi\|_1 < 1$ as the sufficient condition.

nodes.name: Conclude by induction on $k$
nodes.statement: Since each step recovers an optimal atom and OMP never selects the same atom twice, after $m$ steps the algorithm identifies all atoms in the optimal representation.

nodes.name: Exact Recovery for WOMP
nodes.statement: A sufficient condition for WOMP$(\alpha)$ to recover the sparsest representation is $\max_\psi \|\Phi_{\mathrm{opt}}^+ \psi\|_1 < \alpha$, where $\psi$ ranges over columns of $\Psi_{\mathrm{opt}}$.

nodes.name: Exact Recovery for BP (Theorem A, part 2)
nodes.statement: A sufficient condition for BP to recover the sparsest representation of the input signal is the (ERC) condition $\max_\psi \|\Phi_{\mathrm{opt}}^+ \psi\|_1 < 1$, where $\psi$ ranges over atoms not in $\Phi_{\mathrm{opt}}$.
conclusions: BP is correct for $(D,m)$-EXACT-SPARSE whenever (ERC) holds for every $m$-term signal

nodes.name: Strict $\ell_1$ Inequality Lemma
nodes.statement: Suppose $b$ is a vector with nonzero components and $A$ is a matrix whose columns do not have identical $\ell_1$ norms. Then $\|Ab\|_1 < \|A\|_{1,1}\,\|b\|_1$ (strict).

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.3 (Exact Recovery for BP)
nodes.statement: Show that any nonoptimal representation has strictly larger $\ell_1$ norm: split into optimal and nonoptimal atoms, apply Lemma 3.4 with the operator inequality $\|\Phi_{\mathrm{opt}}^+ \Psi_{\mathrm{opt}}\|_{1,1} < 1$ from (ERC), conclude BP picks the optimal coefficients.

nodes.name: Cumulative Coherence Estimate for ERC (Theorem B, part 1)
nodes.statement: Let $\mu_1$ be the cumulative coherence function of $D$. The Exact Recovery Condition holds whenever $\mu_1(m) + \mu_1(m-1) < 1$.
conclusions: The Exact Recovery Condition holds for every $m$-term signal
OMP and BP are correct for $(D,m)$-EXACT-SPARSE

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.5 (Cumulative Coherence Estimate)
nodes.statement: Expand $\Phi_{\mathrm{opt}}^+ = (\Phi_{\mathrm{opt}}^* \Phi_{\mathrm{opt}})^{-1} \Phi_{\mathrm{opt}}^*$, bound $\|\Phi_{\mathrm{opt}}^* \psi\|_1 \leq \mu_1(m)$, develop the inverse as a Neumann series with off-diagonal norm $\leq \mu_1(m-1) < 1$, combine to get the (ERC) bound.

nodes.name: Expand pseudoinverse
nodes.statement: Write $\Phi_{\mathrm{opt}}^+ = (\Phi_{\mathrm{opt}}^* \Phi_{\mathrm{opt}})^{-1} \Phi_{\mathrm{opt}}^*$ and apply the usual operator norm bound to split the estimate into two factors.

nodes.name: Bound second factor by $\mu_1(m)$
nodes.statement: The cumulative coherence directly bounds $\max_\psi \|\Phi_{\mathrm{opt}}^* \psi\|_1 \leq \mu_1(m)$.

nodes.name: Neumann series for inverse
nodes.statement: Decompose $\Phi_{\mathrm{opt}}^* \Phi_{\mathrm{opt}} = I + A$ with off-diagonal $A$ satisfying $\|A\|_{1,1} \leq \mu_1(m-1)$. Whenever $\mu_1(m-1) < 1$, the Neumann series converges and $\|(I+A)^{-1}\|_{1,1} \leq 1/(1 - \mu_1(m-1))$.

nodes.name: Combine and conclude
nodes.statement: Combining the bounds gives $\max_\psi \|\Phi_{\mathrm{opt}}^+ \psi\|_1 \leq \mu_1(m)/(1 - \mu_1(m-1)) < 1$ exactly when $\mu_1(m) + \mu_1(m-1) < 1$. Apply Theorems 3.1 and 3.3.

nodes.name: Coherence-Based ERC Conditions (Theorem B, part 2)
nodes.statement: OMP and BP both recover every superposition of $m$ atoms whenever (i) $(2m-1)\mu < 1$ or, more generally, (ii) $\mu_1(m) + \mu_1(m-1) < 1$.
conclusions: OMP and BP recover every $m$-term superposition

nodes.name: ERC for Multi-ONB (Theorem 3.7)
nodes.statement: If $D$ consists of $L$ concatenated orthonormal bases with overall coherence $\mu$, and the input signal is $s = \sum_{l} s_l$ with $m_l$ atoms from the $l$th basis (assume $m_1 \geq m_2 \geq \cdots$), then the Exact Recovery Condition holds whenever a certain inequality involving $\mu$ and $\{m_l\}$ is satisfied.

nodes.name: ERC for Two-ONB (Corollary 3.8)
nodes.statement: Let $D$ be the union of two orthonormal bases with coherence $\mu$ and the input signal use $p$ atoms from the first basis and $q$ atoms from the second with $p \leq q$. The Exact Recovery Condition holds whenever $2p\mu + (2q-1)\mu < 1$ (Feuer–Nemirovsky-sharp form).

nodes.name: ERC for Multi-ONB ($L$ bases) (Corollary 3.9)
nodes.statement: If $D$ is a $\mu$-coherent dictionary comprised of $L$ orthonormal bases, an inequality (analogous to the two-ONB bound) on the per-basis term counts is sufficient to ensure the Exact Recovery Condition holds for every signal with an $m$-term representation.

nodes.name: Exact Recovery Converse for OMP (Theorem 3.10)
nodes.statement: Assume all $m$-term representations are unique but the Exact Recovery Condition fails for a signal with optimal synthesis matrix $\Phi_{\mathrm{opt}}$. Then there exist signals in the column span of $\Phi_{\mathrm{opt}}$ that OMP cannot recover.
assumptions: (ERC) fails for some signal with optimal synthesis matrix
conclusions: There exist signals OMP cannot recover

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.10 (Converse for OMP)
nodes.statement: If (ERC) fails, choose $\psi$ attaining equality in the bound and select a signal in the column span of $\Phi_{\mathrm{opt}}$ achieving the worst-case ratio; then OMP picks a nonoptimal atom in the first step, ruining recovery.

nodes.name: Sparse Signals Have Measure Zero
nodes.statement: If $m < d$, the collection of signals in $\mathbb{C}^d$ that have an exact representation as a linear combination of $m$ atoms forms a set of Lebesgue measure zero.
conclusions: The set of $m$-sparse signals has Lebesgue measure zero in $\mathbb{C}^d$

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 4.1
nodes.statement: Signals spanned by $m$ distinct atoms form an $m$-dimensional subspace of measure zero. There are finitely many ways to choose $m$ atoms, so the union over all such subspaces is a finite union of measure-zero subspaces, hence measure zero.

nodes.name: General Recovery (Theorem 4.2)
nodes.statement: Assume $\mu_1(m) + \mu_1(m-1) < 1$ and let $a_m^{\mathrm{opt}} = \Phi_{\mathrm{opt}} c_{\mathrm{opt}}$ be an optimal $m$-term approximation of arbitrary $s$. At step $k+1$, OMP recovers another atom from $\Phi_{\mathrm{opt}}$ provided the General Recovery Condition (involving $\|s - a_m^{\mathrm{opt}}\|_2$ and singular values of $\Phi_{\mathrm{opt}}$) holds.
conclusions: At step $k+1$, OMP recovers another atom from $\Phi_{\mathrm{opt}}$ whenever the General Recovery Condition (18) holds

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4.2 (General Recovery)
nodes.statement: Split the greedy ratio into two pieces; bound the first with the operator-norm argument from Section III-C and Lemma 2.3, bound the second with $\|s - a_m^{\mathrm{opt}}\|_2$ via Cauchy–Schwarz; combine to obtain the General Recovery Condition.

nodes.name: Split greedy ratio
nodes.statement: Decompose the residual into the part lying in the column span of $\Phi_{\mathrm{opt}}$ (the deficit term) and the orthogonal complement, splitting the ratio into two factors bounded separately.

nodes.name: Bound first factor (operator-norm)
nodes.statement: Repeat the Section III-C argument: $\max_\psi \|\Phi_{\mathrm{opt}}^+ \psi\|_1 \leq \mu_1(m)/(1 - \mu_1(m-1))$, and bound singular values via Lemma 2.3.

nodes.name: Bound second factor (deficit)
nodes.statement: Use Pythagorean theorem on orthogonal pieces and Cauchy–Schwarz to bound the contribution of the nonsparse part by $\|s - a_m^{\mathrm{opt}}\|_2$ times a term involving $\|\Phi_{\mathrm{opt}}^+\|$.

nodes.name: Combine to General Recovery Condition
nodes.statement: Combine inequalities (21)–(23), use Lemma 2.3 to estimate singular values, derive the explicit condition (18) under which OMP retrieves an optimal atom.

nodes.name: OMP as Approximation Algorithm (Corollary 4.3)
nodes.statement: Assume $\mu_1(m) + \mu_1(m-1) < 1$ and let $s$ be a completely arbitrary signal. Then OMP produces an $m$-term approximant $a_m$ satisfying $\|s - a_m\|_2 \leq C(\mu_1, m)\,\|s - a_m^{\mathrm{opt}}\|_2$ for an explicit constant.
conclusions: OMP yields an $m$-term approximant within an explicit constant factor of optimal

nodes.name: Coherence Form of OMP Approximation (Corollary 4.4 / Theorem C)
nodes.statement: Assume $(2m-1)\mu < 1/3$ or, more generally, $\mu_1(m) + \mu_1(m-1) < 1/2$. Then OMP generates $m$-term approximants $a_m$ satisfying $\|s - a_m\|_2 \leq C\,\|s - a_m^{\mathrm{opt}}\|_2$ with an explicit constant $C$.
conclusions: OMP is an approximation algorithm for $(D,m)$-SPARSE with explicit constant

nodes.name: Approximation Bound for WOMP (Corollary 4.5)
nodes.statement: Weak Orthogonal Matching Pursuit with parameter $\alpha$ calculates $m$-term approximants satisfying an analogous bound $\|s - a_m\|_2 \leq C(\alpha, \mu_1, m)\,\|s - a_m^{\mathrm{opt}}\|_2$.

nodes.name: Sharpness of $\sqrt{m}$ Factor (Remark 4.6)
nodes.statement: The $\sqrt{m}$ factor in (23) is unpleasant but unavoidable without a more subtle approach; an astute reader can lower the factor slightly but the subsequent analysis gains nothing. Stronger bounds are possible under coefficient-distribution assumptions.

nodes.name: Gershgorin Disc Theorem
nodes.statement: Every eigenvalue of a square matrix $A$ lies in at least one of the discs $\{z : |z - a_{ii}| \leq \sum_{j \neq i} |a_{ij}|\}$ in the complex plane.
